extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, STIC search personnel, and other patent classification/search staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for conducting prior-art searches, Internet searches, and Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) allocation during patent examination, including when to consult post-grant proceedings and how to document and prioritize searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tool selection based on examiner knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of search tools is based on the examiner’s knowledge of strengths and weaknesses of the available search tools that are appropriate for use in an examiner’s assigned art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a search tool’s coverage does not meet current search needs, examiner should consider other tools to remedy the deficiency; select tools appropriate to the technology and search needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include NPL and foreign documents when patent documents lag
rubrics_metrics.description: In arts where patent documents lag behind invention (e.g., very active, high-technology arts), searches must include consideration of non-patent literature (NPL) and use tools specialized to cover pertinent NPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners in such arts must take special care to ensure inclusion of NPL and employ effective tools specialized for relevant NPL coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specialized search tools for specialized technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Search needs in some technologies (e.g., chemical structures, DNA sequences) are highly specialized and can only be met through additional use of specific search tools specially constructed and maintained for those needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools that cover domestic patents (including publications), foreign patent documents, and NPL when required by the technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of STIC and trained search personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Because many NPL search tools are numerous and complex, examiners are provided and encouraged to use services of trained professional online search personnel located in Technology Centers’ EICs (STIC) for NPL searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 901.06(a) for services available in STIC; consult STIC staff when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on patent-document-coverage tools in crowded arts
rubrics_metrics.description: In crowded, highly developed arts where claimed inventions are improvements, patent documents (including publications) may serve as the primary reference source; search tool selection may focus on tools providing patent document coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize tools with comprehensive patent document coverage where appropriate for the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine text search with classification/structure searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated search tools usually provide classified and text search capability; text search can be powerful where terminology is well-established, but text search alone is rarely a thorough search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine text search with other criteria (classification, chemical structure, molecular sequence) as a normal expectation in most technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: When text queries are inadequate, use classification browsing
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be difficult to express search needs accurately in textual terms (often in mechanical arts where spatial relationships or shapes matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broader text terms, with or without classification parameters, and traditional browsing of patent documents in relevant classifications when text terms cannot capture the needed aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine search strategy per tool on a case-by-case basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Having determined what search tool(s) should be used, the examiner should determine the appropriate search strategy for each selected tool on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine strategy with consultation with other examiners, supervisory patent examiners, and/or trained search personnel where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Center supplemental guidance and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Technology Center may develop supplemental guidance and training to help examiners acquire specialized skills needed to determine an appropriate field of search in their specific arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training augments general Office-provided training (Office of Patent Training and Search and Information Resources Administration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of search should reflect proper classification locations
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper field of search normally includes the classification locations in which the claimed subject matter would be properly classified at the time of the application's classification or patent grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proper classification corresponds to disclosed but unclaimed embodiments, it is not necessary to search areas with low probability of finding the best references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all relevant groups/subgroups and secondary classification areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Every group/subgroup of CPC and/or class/subclass of the U.S. Patent Classification and other organized systems pertinent to the claimed subject matter should be included, from largest subcombinations to the most elementary part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field of search should extend to all probable areas relevant to claimed subject matter and cover disclosed features likely to be claimed; consult other examiners or supervisors for unfamiliar subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize search areas but consider all probable areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas to be searched should be prioritized so the most likely areas of finding relevant prior art are searched first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although prioritized, a thorough and complete search requires consideration of references from each area where pertinent prior art is likely to be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document field of search and search information
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenting the field of search is required and should follow MPEP § 719.05; see MPEP § 1302.10 for search information printed on patent face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established documentation practices when recording search scope and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a decision-tree methodology for search tool selection
rubrics_metrics.description: While detailed guidance can be Technology Center-specific, a general decision-tree process is suggested for making broad decisions in search tool selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the decision-tree approach to guide broad tool selection decisions and then refine per TC requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet is an approved search tool with confidentiality limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Internet is Office-approved and may be considered when planning/conducting searches, enabling examiners to efficiently locate additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet searches related to unpublished applications MUST be limited to the general state of the art and formulated to protect confidential proprietary IP; non-secure searches that could disclose proprietary information for unpublished applications are NOT permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet searching for published applications allows applicant terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: For published applications, reissue, or reexamination proceedings (not confidential), restrictions on search queries applicable to unpublished apps do not apply and queries may include terminology from applicant’s disclosure and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 707.05(e) for citation of electronic documents and § 719.05 for documenting Internet searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must not solicit assistance or participate on social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may visit social media sites to retrieve public information but are not authorized to participate or solicit assistance (e.g., request users to provide additional info or elaborate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet searching must be limited to information necessary for examination (state of the art, presence/absence of technical features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Internet search strategies per MPEP
rubrics_metrics.description: All Patent Organization users of the Internet for patent application searches must document their search strategies in accordance with established practices (Article 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 719.05 II for documenting Internet searches and general search strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough and complete search commensurate with most detailed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A prerequisite to speedy and just examination is that a thorough and complete search, commensurate with the limitations appearing in the most detailed claims, be made in preparing the first action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first action should be prepared so the second action can be made final or the application allowed with no further searching other than updating the original search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search should anticipate likely claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Search should, insofar as possible, cover all subject matter examiner anticipates might be incorporated into applicant’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can facilitate this by including claims ranging from the broadest to the most detailed they would accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite references useful to forestall presentation of other claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should find and cite references that, while not needed for rejecting claims, would be useful for forestalling presentation of claims to other disclosed subject matter by showing such subject matter is old or obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include references helpful to show prior disclosure even if not strictly necessary for a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the 'best' references and avoid multiplying similar references
rubrics_metrics.description: In selecting references for rejection, examiner should carefully compare references with each other and with the disclosure to avoid unnecessary rejections over similar references; the examiner is to cite only the 'best' references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplying references that add no value increases prosecution burden and should be avoided (see 37 CFR 1.104(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include secondary reference if best reference is vulnerable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the best reference has a publication date making it vulnerable to being overcome under 37 CFR 1.130 or 1.131, and a second reference exists that cannot be overcome and is an adequate basis, the claims should additionally be rejected on that second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add alternative bases for rejection when the primary reference could be overcome by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study full specification of references
rubrics_metrics.description: For all references considered (NPL, foreign, domestic patents), examiner should study the specification/description sufficiently to determine the full value of the reference disclosure relative to claimed or claimable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the full disclosure to evaluate relevance and applicability to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search related post‑grant proceedings when specified conditions met
rubrics_metrics.description: An application under examination is sufficiently related to another proceeding such that a complete search requires review of a post-grant proceeding if any one of enumerated conditions are met (e.g., reissue of a patent previously/currently subject to a post-grant proceeding; benefit claim to a prior US application that issued as a patent previously/currently subject to a post-grant proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any such condition is met, examiner is required to review specific PTAB papers of related post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: When related PTAB proceeding identified, compare claims and consider listed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When a PTAB post-grant proceeding is identified as related, examiner must compare the claims of the examined application with challenged patent claims to determine if they have similar scope or similar claim elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If similar, examiner must consider: Petition; Patent Owner’s Preliminary Response; PTAB’s Decision on Institution (and subsequent Patent Owner responses and Final Written Decision if instituted); any court decisions and subsequent PTAB proceedings; and any parties’ supporting evidence including expert declarations. Document review per MPEP § 719.05 II.A., element L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use professional judgment when there is common inventor/assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examined application shares common inventor or assignee with another application or patent, examiner should exercise professional judgment in determining whether a complete search would include review of the other application/patent and any post-grant proceedings on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider related family or assignee materials when relevant to a complete search.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC hierarchical structure: sections, classes, subclasses, groups, subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC arranges subject matter into hierarchical arrays: Section (highest), Class, Subclass, Main Group and Subgroup; each element is identified by classification symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand each element’s symbol format (e.g., C07D 203/00) and associated titles/definitions when searching/classifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC titles and multipart titles interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The title associated with a CPC symbol defines the scope and is generally read as including titles of all superior organizational units; multipart titles (separated by semicolons) denote distinct, stand-alone coverage entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat semicolon-separated parts as separate entities (e.g., subclass covers multiple distinct things listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: References in CPC titles (parenthetical references)
rubrics_metrics.description: References (parenthetical statements) in titles point to other classification places and apply to the place they appear and all hierarchically lower places unless stated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use references to guide additional classification/search locations of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes, warnings and guidance headings in CPC schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes are supplementary statements applied to the CPC place where they appear (and lower places). Warnings signal deviations from IPC or incomplete classification. Guidance headings may indicate common subject matter across groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult notes, warnings, and guidance headings to understand scope, terminology, limits, and classification rules (e.g., limiting and precedence references).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC definitions must be positive and follow template
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC definitions (for subclasses, main groups, subgroups) must adhere to a definition template and provide a positive description of the subject matter appropriate for the classification place rather than merely restating the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions may include: title, definition statement, references relevant to classification, special classification rules, glossary, and synonyms/keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special classification rules (first place, last place, common rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules govern allocation when a document is classifiable in more than one group: first place priority (highest in scheme), last place priority (lowest), and common rule (classification symbol most completely covering the invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In CPC, the common rule is governing in absence of a specified rule; consult scheme definitions for area-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC database associates symbols to patent families with attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a document is classified in CPC, the symbol is stored as an association to the patent family, so all family members receive the same symbol; each allocation stores attributes including classification symbol, type (invention/additional), and position (first/later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand family-wide effects: a symbol allocation applies to the family and position/type attributes impact retrieval and the 'first' symbol selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention information is mandatory to classify
rubrics_metrics.description: All disclosed invention information in a patent document must be classified in CPC so users can retrieve invention information from the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify all different inventive entities claimed or disclosed (different claims, alternative variants, product vs. method, subcombinations) as invention information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional information is discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information (non-trivial technical information not itself an addition to the state of the art) may be classified on a discretionary basis when useful for search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider classifying constituents, elements, uses, or applications that complement invention information if useful to searchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-STAR (C*) designations for claimed concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: A C* is applied to an allocated symbol when that symbol represents at least one claimed concept; C* designations should be applied regardless of type or position and at least one CPC symbol must be designated C*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allocate new CPC symbols merely to address C*s; designate narrow/specific symbols falling within claimed subject matter as C*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and position attributes for classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each classification allocation has a 'type' attribute (invention or additional) and a 'position' attribute (first or later). The 'first' position is the symbol most adequately representing the invention as a whole for the patent family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is one 'first' per family (first mandatory symbol listed); all other invention or additional allocations are 'later'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to classification: identify subject matter then groups
rubrics_metrics.description: First identify the subject matter to classify, then identify appropriate CPC groups covering that subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow general rules: (A) classify all subject matter covered by claims as invention information (including novel constituents/subcombinations); (B) classify unclaimed novel/unobvious disclosure as invention information; (C) classify additional information that complements invention info if useful; (D) classify novel subcombinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for identifying appropriate CPC groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify candidate subclasses by reviewing titles and definitions, consult subclass notes, references and definitions to verify scope, and repeat the steps to refine group selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scheme and definition guidance to determine required or recommended multi-aspect classification for certain areas; consult notes indicating obligatory classification of aspects.
